headline: South Asia: Former Afghan army member arrested for alleged terrorist activities in Pakistan
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: Former Afghan army member arrested for alleged terrorist activities in Pakistan.
- Africa: Sudan: Sudan War - First Suicide Bombers, Now Long-Range Drone Strikes Are the Norm.

- Military Times, 8 hours ago: Inside Warhound’s plan to engineer a better military working dog.
The company plans to clone top-performing dogs, edit genes associated with health problems and introduce standardized training to puppies as young as two weeks old.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Golding warns against misuse of Speaker’s powers.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 17 hours ago: Golding warns against misuse of Speaker’s powers.
Warning against the gradual erosion of the country’s democracy, Leader of the Opposition Mark Golding has called for the Constitution to be reformed to allow the selection of an independent arbiter to preside over parliamentary affairs. Referencing recent amendments to Barbados’ constitution, Golding said the change reversed the practice of selecting a Speaker from among members of Parliament and instead chose an independent person from outside the Parliament to preside over the sittings.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Former Afghan army member arrested for alleged terrorist activities in Pakistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Former Afghan army member arrested for alleged terrorist activities in Pakistan.
PESHAWAR: Security forces and law enforcement agencies have arrested a man formerly associated with the Afghan National Army (ANA) for allegedly carrying out terrorist activities in Pakistan, it emerged on Wednesday. At a media briefing, Additional Inspector (AIG) General Abbas Ahsan of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police claimed the suspect, identified as Hikmatullah alias Hamza, was arrested during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber district’s Tirah valley. “The suspect was arrested on November 7.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Iran slams 'repugnant' $20m US reward for nuclear information.
Iran hit out at the United States’ $20 million reward for information on its nuclear programme on Wednesday, calling it “repugnant and regrettable”. Tehran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged the International Atomic Energy Agency and the UN Security Council to condemn the reward, which was announced last week. Last Friday, the US military said up to $20 million and “possible relocation” were available for information about the programme’s “facilities, equipment, and associated personnel”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: 10 cops martyred, 18 terrorists killed as police party comes under attack in KP's Kohat.
PESHAWAR: Eighteen terrorists were killed while 10 cops were martyred on Wednesday when the police team came under attack on its way back after completing an operation against elements involved in illegal gold mining, police said. In a statement, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police public relations director said the personnel were conducting a joint operation with the local civil administration in the Darabukach locality near Kohat city.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Jerusalem Post, just now: US envoys to meet Putin, Zelensky after Russia-Ukraine war talks in Abu Dhabi.
United States envoys will separately meet Russia’s Vladimir Putin and Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday as they seek to seize “openings” from two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on ending the Ukraine war. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel first to Moscow to meet the Russian president, before flying to Dublin — where Zelensky will attend European meetings — to debrief the Ukrainian leader. The countries agreed in Abu Dhabi to a major prisoner exchange — the “biggest” ever, according to Kushner — though no side gave any figures.

The 49-year-old contract soldier from Java was captured in the frontline Zaporizhzhia region after entering Ukrainian-held territory following a drone strike on his Russian unit, The Guardian reported, citing Kyiv’s state-backed “I Want to Live” surrender initiative. Hopes had been low for any significant development in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations. China’s infantry units are adapting to the growing threat from drones, with some brigades introducing compulsory counter-drone training, new equipment and fresh tactics to help soldiers evade aerial surveillance and attacks. The latest example comes from a brigade of the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) 75th Group Army, which has made counter-drone training compulsory after an exercise exposed how troops relying on traditional camouflage were vulnerable to drone-directed artillery...

Slain Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung was killed by her ex-husband in a fit of rage after she hurled insults at him during a car ride, his elder brother has told a court. In a tearful confession in the High Court on Wednesday, Anthony Kwong Kong-kit said his younger brother, Alex Kwong Kong-chi, had fatally attacked Choi on February 21, 2023, but stressed that there had been no plan to kill her beforehand.
